is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae sensu lato (s.l.) mosquitoes (Abstract, page 1).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study reports on Vgsc L1014F (L995F) and Ace-1 G119S (G280S) mutations (Table 1, page 6).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 1 on page 6 provides allele frequencies for L1014F and G119S for An. gambiae s.s., An. coluzzii, and An. arabiensis, with a total sample size of 100 mosquitoes (page 5).

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected as larvae from Kpalsogu, a village in the Northern region of Ghana (Abstract, page 1; Study site, page 2).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study reporting original bioassay and genotyping results.

sub_country_location.evidence: The study was conducted in Kpalsogu village, Kumbungu District, northern Ghana (page 2).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Mosquito larvae were sampled from April 2021 to August 2021 (page 2).

duplicate_risk.evidence: While the study mentions support from the PMI VectorLink project for insectary facilities, the collection and analysis appear specific to this study in Kpalsogu.

supplement.evidence: All relevant data, including species composition and marker frequencies, are contained within the main text and tables of the article.

assessment.summary: The study reports the baseline susceptibility of Anopheles gambiae s.l. to clothianidin in Kpalsogu, northern Ghana, following the introduction of SumiShield 50WG for IRS. Mosquitoes were collected as larvae between April and August 2021. The study identifies An. gambiae s.s., An. coluzzii, and An. arabiensis and reports high frequencies of the Vgsc L1014F (L995F) mutation and moderate frequencies of the Ace-1 G119S (G280S) mutation across these species.
